channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: Times Square Collective Showcase — February 2027 · Arrival Gallery
item.description:
Arrival Gallery is selling places in a one-day digital billboard showcase on a screen at 1568 Broadway in Times Square, New York, on 15 February 2027. The work is shown as a curated rotation of artists, each piece in a 1:1 square format throughout the day. Each artist enters one artwork as a JPG or PNG (the upload step also accepts MP4), and work that is not square is centre-cropped. Work showing smoking, violence, nudity, vulgarity or offensive content is not accepted.
The application form charges £100 including VAT as its last, required step, and says that only completed payments guarantee a place on the billboard; it describes the showcase as 20 artists. Arrival Gallery's own digital showcases page gives different terms: 10 artist slots at £160 per slot, applications reviewed before places are confirmed, and no payment collected through the application forms. The form is branded Art Seen New York and, once submitted, sends applicants to art-seen.com.
The deadline is 31 January 2027, 23:59 GMT. — Deadline: January 31, 2027. Fee: £100 (£160 per slot on gallery page). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: SPREADS Magazine — January 2027 Issue · Arrival Gallery
item.description:
SPREADS is an artist magazine published by Arrival Gallery, which runs group showcases in London, New York, Athens, Paris, Milan and other cities. It comes out four times a year, on 1 January, 1 April, 1 July and 1 October, as a free digital edition and as a printed copy sold through the print-on-demand service Peecho, and it sets artists' work alongside the ideas, materials and stories behind it. This call is for the January 2027 issue and is open to artists anywhere, in all visual disciplines.
Applying is free, but artists who take up a placement in the magazine pay a publication fee. The amount is not given on the SPREADS website, on Arrival Gallery's open-calls page or in the latest back issue.
Applying starts with a mailing-list signup: the application link asks for a first name and email address and then gives access to the submission form. The magazine asks applicants to choose the images that speak most clearly about their practice and to introduce themselves and the ideas, materials or questions behind the work. The deadline covers the whole of 5 December, London time. Later issues follow the same pattern, with deadlines on 5 March, 5 June and 5 September. — Deadline: December 5, 2026. Fee: Free (publication fee if selected, amount not published). Prize: Publication.

item.title: 7th AOYF Human Rights Photography Prize
item.description: The first fully international edition of a prize the Geneva foundation Act On Your Future has run since 2015 with the Centre de la photographie Genève — until now open only to students and recent graduates of six European art schools, and from this seventh edition open to artists anywhere. The 2027 theme is Post-Truth: Reality in Question. The call asks what can be believed and who shapes the reality we see at a moment when images circulate instantly, algorithms decide what reaches us, AI can generate content hard to tell from a photograph, and authentic images and victims' testimony can themselves be dismissed as fabricated. Projects may engage evidence and testimony, manipulated or AI-generated imagery, contested histories, propaganda, the circulation of images, or personal experience of a reality others dispute; documentary, conceptual, experimental and interdisciplinary approaches are all invited and no photographic style is privileged. Five finalists are chosen by an interdisciplinary jury over three rounds — two online rounds in January and February 2027, notification in February, final deliberations in Geneva on 14 June 2027 — and show together at the CPG from 16 June to 21 August 2027. The winner, announced at the opening on 16 June, receives CHF 10,000: CHF 7,000 unrestricted plus a CHF 3,000 project development grant. The other four finalists each receive CHF 1,000. All five get curatorial guidance from the CPG team, up to CHF 1,500 of production support produced in Geneva under CPG supervision, and travel and accommodation to attend the final jury round, award ceremony and opening from 14 to 16 June 2027, subject to budget. Each finalist also donates two works made with that production support to the AOYF Collection, chosen by mutual agreement: copyright stays with the artist, but ownership of those physical works passes to the foundation, which may exhibit, reproduce, lend or sell them from its collection with the artist credited. Works shown in the exhibition may be offered for sale by agreement with the artist, and proceeds from any sale are shared equally between artist and foundation. Being in Geneva from 14 to 16 June 2027 is an undertaking finalists give, with remote participation only exceptionally authorised, and visas are the artist's own responsibility, their fees covered subject to approval and budget. Entry is free and open to artists aged 18 and over, individuals or collectives, with no restriction on nationality, residence or formal art education. One project per applicant: 8 to 25 images (or a moving-image work or excerpt up to 10 minutes), a project statement of up to 300 words, a 150-word biography with contact details, and captions. Work may be new, ongoing, completed, previously exhibited or published. Generated, composited, staged, appropriated and archival material is allowed provided the methods are disclosed in the statement — passing manipulated or generated material off as documentary evidence can disqualify. AOYF and the CPG may ask for raw files, metadata, prompts or reference material to verify authorship, and failing to supply what they reasonably request can disqualify too. Applications close 20 December 2026 at 23:59 CET and are accepted only through Picter. CAUTION: the foundation's own prix-de-photographie page says nothing about this edition — re-read on 28 October 2026 it still presents the 2023 prize, open only to students and graduates of six partner art schools and paying each of the four non-winning finalists CHF 500, under a 2023 copyright line — so the organiser's prospectus and terms and conditions on Picter are the surfaces that bind here. — Deadline: December 20, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: CHF 10,000 + CHF 1,000 ×4 + Exhibition.

item.title: Women United Art Magazine — Issue XVI
item.description: The Winter 2027 issue of an international quarterly print and digital magazine dedicated to women in the arts, distributed worldwide through Amazon. The entry form states the scope in the organiser's own words: open to all women artists regardless of age, experience, education, race, sexual orientation or location, and specifically focused on painting, drawing, printmaking, photography, digital art, collage, fibre and textile art, sculpture and installation. Selected artists are featured in Issue XVI in either the In The Spotlight or The Curator's Pick section — the editors decide the length — plus a social media feature and a complimentary digital copy; artists picked for In The Spotlight are contacted with further questions about their work and practice. Everyone who submits receives a complimentary digital copy, and artists not selected for this issue may submit to the following one free of charge. The entry fee is a self-assessed sliding scale with no proof asked for: €35 standard for artists with stable income, institutional support or grant funding, €25 reduced for early-career or freelance artists, the underemployed and those carrying unpaid care responsibilities, and €15 symbolic for art students and artists facing economic or structural limitations. The magazine says the fees fund waivers for artists who need them, and asks only that you choose the tier that genuinely reflects your situation. Prepare an artist bio and an artist statement of up to 300 words each and between two and four images at a minimum of 300 DPI, cropped and ready for print. Entries close 10 December 2026, selected artists are notified by email on 20 December 2026 and the issue publishes in January or February 2027. Editor-in-Chief is Mona Lerch, who founded Women United ART MOVEMENT in 2021 and also runs its year-long artist residency and mentorship programme. Note the symbolic tier has risen from €10 at Issue XV to €15 for this issue. — Deadline: December 10, 2026. Fee: €15–€35. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Annual Holiday Gift Show · Gallery Seven
item.description: Gallery Seven's annual selling show in Lockport, Illinois, hung from 27 November 2026 to 8 January 2027 and built around the town's Christmas in the Square weekend — the gallery opens with an artists' reception and holiday open house on Saturday 28 November, 12–5pm, and holds a second open house on Thursday 3 December, 5–7pm. The submission form is a one-page PDF on the gallery's own site and asks only for your details, your medium, the number of pieces and a price range; selection is made from three example images emailed to the gallery, and there is no entry fee. The medium line on the form is a blank to fill in and nothing excludes photography — the gallery's own list of what it shows opens with Photography, ahead of pen and ink, oil painting, assemblage, watercolour, woodturning and jewellery. Work sells on a signed consignment contract with a 30% commission to the gallery, which leaves the artist 70%. This is a hand-delivered show: everything must be priced, labelled and photo-inventoried by 21 November, with drop-off on 21 November 12–5pm or 22 November 12–3pm and pick-up on 9 or 10 January. Distance, not medium, is the real gate — the gallery asks for work by local artists and its stated mission is to give local artists somewhere to show and sell. Gallery Seven began in 2007 as a group of seven fine-art photographers in Joliet and moved into the historic Gaylord Building in downtown Lockport in 2018; it runs two juried shows a year, one of which, Open Lens, has been its fine-art photography exhibition every June since 2010. — Deadline: November 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition + 70% of sales.

item.title: 2026 Bob & Millie Lynn Grant · National Press Photographers Foundation
item.description: A $5,000 grant from the National Press Photographers Foundation for a long-term documentary project photographed in the United States — work that takes a creative approach to important stories that might otherwise go untold, with the emphasis on ethical, narrative-driven journalism and on underreported or overlooked aspects of American society. It is named for Bob Lynn, who was assistant managing editor for graphics at The Virginian-Pilot and its photojournalism leader for 17 years, wrote Vision, Courage & Heart, and received the NPPA's Joseph Sprague Memorial Award. Judges weigh the strength and impact of the storytelling alongside image sequencing, technical quality and adherence to professional photojournalism standards; no juror is named. Both students and working professionals may apply, provided they are legally authorized to work in the United States, Puerto Rico or the US Minor Outlying Islands, and the funded work must be photographed in the US. You submit up to 24 images or three video stories, a project proposal, a budget and a short resume; entries can be edited up to the deadline, ongoing and collaborative projects are eligible, and existing publication deals must be disclosed. Two funding bars are published, on two different surfaces: the grant page excludes anyone who has received more than $10,000 in other funding in the past three years, and the application form excludes anyone who has had more than $5,000 in grant funding in the three years before the deadline. Staff photographers need written permission from their employer first. AI imagery is barred outright and using it to make images or video disqualifies the entry. There is no entry fee. Payment comes in two parts: $4,000 on award, then $1,000 on delivery of at least 25 captioned high-resolution images within 18 months, with a written account of the completed work due in 12 to 18 months and monthly check-ins with an NPPF coordinator throughout. Recent recipients include Bob Miller, Ed Kashi, Laura Morton, Caitlin O'Hara, Kathy Shorr, Mary Calvert and Nathan Posner. Applications run through Picter and the deadline line reads 4:59pm on 30 November, so treat the afternoon, not midnight, as the cutoff. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $5,000.

item.title: Creators’ Favourite Sluts: A Two-Spirit/Indigiqueer Art Market · grunt gallery
item.description: grunt gallery in Vancouver is bringing back “Creators’ Favourite Sluts”, the Two-Spirit/Indigiqueer art market it first ran in February for Valentine’s Day, for a second edition on Saturday 12 December 2026, and is looking for 2S and/or Queer Indigenous artists from Turtle Island and Palestine to join the roster of tabling artists. It is presented by Vance Wright with the gallery. Applying is not the same as being selected: the intake form says official selections are made at the end of October and that every applicant is told where they stand then, and applications close at 11:59pm on 31 October. The market takes over two rooms of the gallery and there is space for 13 to 15 artists, so most tablers will share a table two to one — you are asked to think honestly about how much table space your work actually needs, and to say in the application if you need more, since the more artists are willing to share the more can be included. grunt provides the tables and chairs; artists handle their own transactions and keep 100% of their proceeds. There is no fee to apply and no fee for the table. The form asks every applicant for three to five images of their work and a bio of up to 100 words, plus pronouns and a short description of what you plan to sell. Neither the call nor the form uses the word photography: what the form asks for is “a short description of the artwork or wares you plan on selling”, offering “beadwork, paintings, prints, stickers, etc.” as its examples, so a photographer with prints or zines applies on the same footing as any other maker. The market runs 1pm to 7pm with load-in from 12:30pm, and grunt says to get in touch if those hours do not work for you. Access information for the space is published at the foot of grunt’s events page, and the gallery invites specific access questions by email. What is on offer is a free table at an artist-run centre that has been in Vancouver since 1984, in front of its audience, with nothing taken off the top. — Deadline: October 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: None listed.

item.title: 2027 Black Artist Showcase · Jamestown Settlement
item.description: Jamestown Settlement, the living-history museum run by the Jamestown-Yorktown Foundation near the site of England's first permanent North American colony, invites adult Black visual artists living in Virginia to submit work for its 2027 Black Artist Showcase, hung along the Great Hall passageways that lead into the museum's main galleries from 30 January to 28 March 2027. The theme is "Founders and Foundations", and the call is open to any medium — the museum's own listing names painting, drawing, printmaking, graphic arts and photography — which makes this one of the few state-museum exhibition slots a photographer can reach without an entry fee of any kind. Up to three works may be submitted on the museum's own web form, each needing a title, medium, accurate framed dimensions and a reference JPEG or PNG under 5 MB. Selected artists are notified by 16 November 2026 and sign a Memorandum of Agreement with the Foundation, which pays a small honorarium at the close of the showcase; artists must return a signed Virginia substitute W-9 by 30 December 2026 or their work cannot be hung. Work is delivered in person to Jamestown Settlement between 11 and 24 January 2027, by appointment, and must arrive exhibition-ready: works on paper glazed and framed, hanging hardware already installed, D-rings preferred to wire. The Foundation states plainly that it will not prepare, mount, frame or fit hardware to any work, and that anything arriving not exhibit-ready is dropped from the showcase. Two public events sit inside the run: the "After Angelo" daytime celebration of African American heritage on 20 February 2027, where showcase artists may reserve a vendor table and sell their own work, and a "Last Looks" closing reception on the evening of 27 March 2027. Artists collect their work between 3 and 10 April 2027. — Deadline: November 4, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Museum exhibition + honorarium.

item.title: Call for Curators: The Gallery at the Attucks 2027 · Norfolk Arts
item.description: Norfolk Arts, the City of Norfolk's municipal arts agency, is looking for a curator to build the 2027 exhibition at The Gallery at the Attucks — the gallery inside the Attucks Theatre on Church Street, built in 1919 and described by Norfolk Arts as the oldest remaining Black-owned and Black-built theatre in the United States. The brief asks for a group exhibition of at least seven artists with a connection to Hampton Roads, in contemporary 2-D work only, that speaks to the Attucks' cultural legacy; Norfolk Arts says Black curators are strongly encouraged to apply. Proposals are expected to set out a clear strategy for drawing large and diverse audiences, and partnerships, cross-disciplinary ideas and additional programming — artist talks, performances, demonstrations — are preferred. The money is real and unusually transparent for a municipal call: $1,500 goes to the curator and $3,500 is divided among the exhibiting artists, there is no application fee, and the gallery takes no commission on sales, which artists may choose to allow or not. The show runs for six months in a space of roughly 1,500 square feet. Because this is a city contract, the curator and the participating artists each upload a W-9 and register as a City of Norfolk vendor to be paid. The curator may not exhibit their own work, which makes this a genuine curatorial commission rather than a route to a self-made show — and for photographers, a 2-D-only brief in a six-month municipal gallery slot is one of the few places a Hampton Roads practice can be seen at that length. Materials are emailed to Norfolk Arts by 11:59pm on 8 December 2026; the agency publishes a full prospectus PDF alongside the call. Curators are notified by 8 January 2027 and the first exhibition installs in mid-April 2027. — Deadline: December 8, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $1,500 curator stipend + $3,500 artist stipends + 6-month exhibition.

item.title: Art in Transit Open Call for Artwork · WMATA Art in Transit
item.description: Metro's Office of Community Engagement runs a standing, no-fee open call to build a pool of artists whose work can be placed across the Washington transit system — and photography is one of the nine disciplines it names explicitly, not an afterthought. Five formats are on offer. Barricade and construction-wall art turns the temporary barriers around station works into large-scale vinyl wraps or printed panels, so files need to arrive in a modifiable digital format suitable for vinyl, corrugated plastic or aluminium. Digital screen activations put photography, animation and other digital media on screens throughout stations, transit hubs and Metro facilities, with a twenty-second run-time cap and a requirement that the work can be reformatted for custom screen sizes. Station and facility installations are temporary exhibitions in mezzanines, corridors and other public-facing spaces, two- or three-dimensional, on view for up to three years. The remaining two routes cover community and special-event activations — commemorations, cultural celebrations, anniversary programmes — and a catch-all for new spaces and technologies as they appear. Eligibility is regional and clearly stated: artists and creatives resident in the District of Columbia, Maryland and Virginia, aged 18 or over, working individually or in teams, with priority to artists inside Metro's registered service area; emerging, mid-career and established practitioners are all invited, and Metro says artists from historically underrepresented communities are strongly encouraged to apply. The application is one form asking for a 50-word bio, a 100-word statement, five work samples as JPEG or PNG, a portfolio or social link and a CV of no more than two pages. Submissions go to the Art in Transit programme team and stay on file for current and future opportunities; for multi-year temporary projects a Community Advisory Group of Metro staff, local residents and regional public-art specialists may be convened for the final choice. Selection is not guaranteed by applying, but if a project does come, the artist submits a quote and Metro provides a budget covering the artist fee and any file-preparation labour. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: Free. Prize: Artist fee from a project budget + temporary exhibition.

item.title: Exhibition Proposals: Main and Nano Galleries · DC Arts Center
item.description: The DC Arts Center in Adams Morgan takes exhibition proposals and bodies of work from artists and curators year-round, for both of its newly renovated galleries: the Main Gallery, roughly 700 square feet and built for full-size work in any medium, and the Nano Gallery, roughly 125 square feet for small-format work that hangs easily. You can indicate which space suits your work, but DCAC makes the final placement call. What makes this one worth understanding before applying is that DCAC is explicitly curator-driven: an accepted application does not book you a show, it puts you on the centre's roster of approved exhibiting artists, whose materials the curatorial team reviews when planning future exhibitions. From there a curator may pick up an already-curated proposal as submitted, pull one or more pieces from your submitted body of work into a group show, or pair you with a curator from DCAC's roster to shape the proposal together — and if a curator is interested, the next step is a studio visit. DCAC is candid that this stage moves on the gallery's own schedule, quickly or slowly, and that your work stays active in the system either way. Unsuccessful applicants are told so and are sent the committee's feedback, with an invitation to apply again once it has been worked through. The application needs an artist statement and biography, a résumé, proposed exhibition title and description, an image or video list, and high-resolution files that show the work as you intend it to be exhibited. The fee is $25, waived for DCAC Artist Members. Proposals are reviewed quarterly by the Visual Arts Committee, which judges artistic quality, conceptual coherence, readiness for exhibition, growth potential, alignment with DCAC's mission, and marketability. Artists keep 60% of the sale price on work sold, or 70% as Artist Members. DCAC states it supports artists at all stages of their careers and across all disciplines, welcomes applications from all artists, and does not discriminate on any basis. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: $25 (free for DCAC Artist Members). Prize: Gallery exhibition + 60–70% of sales.

item.title: FeelsZine Issue 28 — Play
item.description: FEELS is a Canadian independent zine that has published two issues a year, in January and July, since Issue 01 in January 2017, and Issue 28 takes "Play" as its theme — the mission statement for it is still being written, which leaves the brief unusually open for anyone submitting early. The zine is deliberately multidisciplinary: photography sits alongside illustration, art, collage, comics and typography, and those run next to poetry, personal essays, fiction and interview proposals. Pitches for something not on that list are explicitly welcomed. Every accepted submission earns a $60 honorarium and a free copy of the issue, which is a real rate for a small independent publication and a meaningful change from the $25 the zine paid for Issue 27. Submission is free and goes by email with a short bio, a description of the work, and a statement of your personal connection to the issue topic — FEELS prioritises stories and art grounded in lived experience. Photographic and art submissions need a short artist statement; the zine is printed at 6.5 × 9.5 inches with a 0.125-inch bleed, low-res proofs are fine to submit, and accepted work is requested at 300dpi for print. Writing is capped at 1,800 words for longform, two poems or less unless part of a single collection of up to four. The editors ask for one or two works per person given submission volume, and promise to reply to every email. Previously published work is accepted so long as it will not appear in another Canadian independent magazine during the same six-month publication window, with attribution included if the original publisher requires it. FEELS publishes a majority of Canadian content as a Canadian publication but does include global contributors, and the call states plainly that it welcomes and encourages people of all diverse experiences, abilities and communities. The zine is also explicit about machine-made work: "We are an anti-AI publication and do not accept any pieces using generative AI." The deadline is 15 March 2027 and the issue is released in July 2027. — Deadline: March 15, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication + $60 honorarium.

item.title: Call for Curatorial & Exhibition Proposals · Art Works Downtown
item.description: Art Works Downtown, the 501(c)(3) non-profit arts organisation whose 40,000-square-foot building at 1325-1337 Fourth Street in downtown San Rafael houses galleries and 33 artist studios, takes proposals on a rolling basis for Gallery 1337, its primary exhibition space. The invitation is deliberately wide: emerging and established curators, independent curators, artists, and collaborative teams may propose solo or group exhibitions, and AWD says it is looking for "projects with a clear vision, strong artistic quality, professionalism, originality, and a compelling concept suited to the gallery and our public audience." What makes this worth a photographer's or curator's time is that AWD budgets for the work the proposal implies rather than simply lending a wall: selected projects may receive up to $5,000 in curatorial or exhibition support, use of Gallery 1337, exhibition planning and production support, advertising and promotion, gallery staffing during public hours (Wednesday to Saturday, 11am to 5pm), two exhibition receptions, and support for related public programs. There is no application fee. A proposal should carry the exhibition title; a curatorial or exhibition statement setting out concept, themes and goals; curator and/or artist bio and CV; participating artists with brief bios and portfolio links if they are already identified; representative artwork images with artist, title, medium, dimensions, date and price where applicable; the proposed number and type of works; an installation concept with any technical or equipment needs; preferred dates and timeline; public programming ideas; audience, outreach or partnership ideas; and a preliminary budget naming the intended use of any requested stipend. Proposals are weighed on strength and originality of concept, quality of artwork, professionalism and completeness, feasibility, appropriate scale and quantity, ability to engage a broad public audience, inclusivity, diversity, equity, accessibility and representation, and the potential for meaningful public programs. Photographic work is squarely inside the artwork guidelines — AWD primarily exhibits original artwork and permits signed and numbered limited editions, while un-editioned reproductions and print-to-order works are generally not accepted; video and new media are welcome, though most equipment must come from the artist or curator, audio normally needs headphones, and projection may be limited by ambient light. Explicit sexual content and graphic violence are not eligible. Artists should generally reside within 100 miles of San Rafael unless otherwise approved. At least half the exhibited work should be available for sale; AWD processes sales and the tax, keeping 40% of the retail price and paying 60% to the artist unless something else is agreed in writing. Proposals go by email to the exhibitions contact, with no phone calls; AWD warns that the volume of submissions means it may not answer every applicant and cannot give individual critiques, and that it will reach out directly where a proposal fits an upcoming slot. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: Free. Prize: Up to $5,000 + exhibition.

item.title: FUTURES Baltic Talents 2027 · ISSP
item.description: ISSP, the Riga-based photography institution that has been the Baltic member of the FUTURES Photography Platform since 2022, is looking for three artists from Latvia, Lithuania and Estonia to join the platform's 2027 cohort. FUTURES was founded in 2018 with support from the EU's Creative Europe Culture programme and now pools the talent programmes of twenty leading European photography institutions, each nominating new artists every year. Selected artists receive a participation grant of €500; conversations with international professionals, online and in person; an invitation to the FUTURES Annual Event in autumn 2027 with travel and accommodation covered; access to an online learning programme run with Magnum Photos; the chance to apply to the platform's internal open call for the travelling Annual Exhibition; the chance to apply for a funded FUTURES residency and a tutoring session; invitations to events hosted by the platform's other members; and an artist page plus promotion through the FUTURES website, social media and annual publication. Access to the Magnum learning programme, the FUTURES Conversations, the annual exhibition call, the residency call, the artist page and the member invitations all continue in the years that follow. Three conditions have to hold: you are based in or come from Latvia, Lithuania or Estonia — citizenship or official residency status in one of the three countries — you can show dedication and continuity in your practice over at least three years including at least one exhibition, and you can submit a strong photographic work made in the last three years. Artists who applied in previous years are invited to apply again. The application is free: a Google Form with a PDF of one recent project, due at midnight EET on 6 December 2026. The selection committee is ISSP's own programme and managing directors together with an Estonian and a Lithuanian colleague, and it weighs who would benefit most from the platform's exposure, networking and learning. Selected candidates are notified by 20 December and must have a CV, a portrait and fifteen low- and high-resolution images ready by 1 January. — Deadline: December 6, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €500.

item.title: WC Gallery Installation Proposals · New Hampshire Art Association
item.description: The oddest room in the New Hampshire Art Association's Portsmouth gallery is its bathroom, and the association runs it as an exhibition space. In the association's words the WC Gallery is "an irregular installation space" and it is looking for artists "exploring innovative ideas and taking creative risks to create a visually and mentally stimulating experience". Installations run in three intervals a year — February–May, June–August and September–December — and the brief is to keep the bathroom functional while making it immersive and actively engaging for visitors: a mural or wall work, found objects, or any idea that transforms the room. NHAA publishes a photograph and a dimensioned diagram of the space and encourages artists to come and see it in person. Proposals are accepted on a rolling basis and artists may submit more than one. A proposal is a one-page plan with a diagram showing images or drawings of what will go where, the materials involved (paint, hung work, 3D objects), what the artist will need from the gallery (pedestals, labels), a title, preferred months of installation, and a timeline of what is already made and what will be. Open to regional artists, NHAA members and non-members alike, and free to propose. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: Free. Prize: Solo exhibition.

item.title: Versions of Me: The Artist as Subject · Praxis Photo Arts Center
item.description: Juried exhibition at Praxis Gallery in Minneapolis on the artist as subject. The gallery's framing: the self-portrait has long offered artists a means of exploring identity, experimenting with representation and recording their presence in the world, and in photography the artist becomes both observer and observed, making an image that may reveal, conceal, question or reinvent the self. Praxis seeks work ranging from direct studies of the face and body to reflections, shadows, staged encounters, assumed identities, objects, environments and traces of presence — interpretations of self-portraiture that express, suggest or complicate our understanding of the person who made it. Up to 38 photographs are selected for the physical gallery show (19 December 2026 – 9 January 2027), featured on the gallery's online exhibition page and permanently archived there. Awards are a Directors' Choice (free entry into two future juried calls of the artist's choice) and five honourable mentions featured in the exhibition, the printed exhibition catalogue and the online gallery. Entrants must be 18 or older, and images shown at Praxis within the past year are ineligible. Praxis members get 10 images for the price of 5, and artists experiencing financial hardship may request a free submission from the gallery. Selected artists either ship an unframed original print or use the gallery's optional $37 printing service; Praxis provides all matting and framing in its 22 × 22-inch black frames and retains a 50% commission on any print sales. Notification is 27 November 2026. — Deadline: November 15, 2026. Fee: $35 (5 images) + $5 each additional. Prize: Exhibition + catalog.

item.title: London Showcase · HUGE Gallery
item.description:
This call is for HUGE Gallery's London showcase at The Factory, 21–31 Shacklewell Lane, London E8, from 27 to 29 November 2026. HUGE Gallery runs three-day group showcases in several cities and describes itself as an open exhibition platform for emerging artists. It is open to emerging, independent, self-taught and formally trained artists working in any medium, photography included, and artists do not need to live locally or attend.
Applying is free, but places are paid for by the artists who are selected. Physical places start at £150 and digital places at £50. A physical place includes presentation in the venue, an artist page on HUGE's website for two years, documentation and a social media feature; a digital place covers on-screen and online presentation. HUGE's own pitch is "If it fits, you're in".
Applying starts with a mailing-list signup: the application link asks for a first name and email address, says applications are not public, and sends access to the form by email. — Deadline: November 16, 2026. Fee: Free (£150+ physical, £50+ digital if selected). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Paris Showcase · HUGE Gallery
item.description:
This call is for HUGE Gallery's Paris showcase at 18 rue Lally Tollendal, Paris, from 5 to 7 February 2027. HUGE Gallery runs three-day group showcases in several cities and describes itself as an open exhibition platform for emerging artists. It is open to emerging, independent, self-taught and formally trained artists working in any medium, photography included, and artists do not need to live locally or attend.
Applying is free, but places are paid for by the artists who are selected. The Paris listing does not print its prices; HUGE's general terms are from £150 for a physical place and from £50 for a digital one. A physical place includes presentation in the venue, an artist page on HUGE's website for two years, documentation and a social media feature; a digital place covers on-screen and online presentation. HUGE's own pitch is "If it fits, you're in".
Applying starts with a mailing-list signup: the application link asks for a first name and email address, says applications are not public, and sends access to the form by email. — Deadline: January 20, 2027. Fee: Free (£150+ physical, £50+ digital if selected). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Lyon Showcase · HUGE Gallery
item.description:
This call is for HUGE Gallery's Lyon showcase at 53 Cours Tolstoï in Villeurbanne, on the edge of Lyon, from 4 to 6 December 2026. HUGE Gallery runs three-day group showcases in several cities and describes itself as an open exhibition platform for emerging artists. It is open to emerging, independent, self-taught and formally trained artists working in any medium, photography included, and artists do not need to live locally or attend.
Applying is free, but places are paid for by the artists who are selected. For Lyon, physical places start at £100 and digital places at £45. A physical place includes presentation in the venue, an artist page on HUGE's website for two years, documentation and a social media feature; a digital place covers on-screen and online presentation. HUGE's own pitch is "If it fits, you're in".
Applying starts with a mailing-list signup: the application link asks for a first name and email address, says applications are not public, and sends access to the form by email. — Deadline: November 18, 2026. Fee: Free (£100+ physical, £45+ digital if selected). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Tokyo 2027 · HUGE Gallery
item.description:
This call is for HUGE Gallery's Tokyo showcase at Design Festa Gallery Harajuku WEST, from 5 to 7 March 2027. HUGE Gallery runs three-day group showcases in several cities and describes itself as an open exhibition platform for emerging artists. It is open to emerging, independent, self-taught and formally trained artists working in any medium, photography included, and artists do not need to live locally or attend.
Applying is free, but places are paid for by the artists who are selected. For Tokyo, physical places start at £300 and digital places at £80. A physical place includes presentation in the venue, an artist page on HUGE's website for two years, documentation and a social media feature; a digital place covers on-screen and online presentation. HUGE's own pitch is "If it fits, you're in". The Tokyo application form adds that exhibition spaces are limited and allocated on a first-come, first-served basis.
Unlike HUGE's European shows, Tokyo applications go straight to a Typeform without a mailing-list step. — Deadline: February 25, 2027. Fee: Free (£300+ physical, £80+ digital if selected). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Contradiction · Sebastopol Center for the Arts
item.description:
A juried exhibition at Sebastopol Center for the Arts built on paradox. The call asks for work that lives in the tension between opposing forces rather than resolving it: "Consider how things that shouldn't belong together insist on being together. Consider an enigma, a paradox. Bitter/sweet, organized chaos, strange bedfellows. What happens when fire meets ice, big meets little, or grief meets joy?" SebArts offers a list of starting points - bitter and sweet, fire and ice, grief and joy, dark and light, sun and moon, logic and imagination, life and death, opposites on the colour wheel - and states that the work "doesn't need to resolve the tension. It needs to inhabit it." The show runs 27 February to 11 April 2027 at the centre's gallery in Sebastopol, with an opening reception on 27 February, 2-4pm.
SebArts invites "artists working in any medium", so photographic work is eligible, and the organisation adds that it welcomes "artists of all backgrounds and perspectives". Awards are $300 for first place, $200 for second, $100 for third, and two $50 coordinator awards. Work sold during the exhibition splits 60% to the artist and 40% to SebArts. Jurors are listed as TBA; jurying runs 7-14 January 2027 and artists are notified by email on 15 January 2027.
Entry is online only, at $35 for a first application and $10 each for a second and third - a maximum of three separate submissions, each entered one at a time, with up to three JPEG images of 5MB or less per entry. Work must not have been shown previously in the SebArts gallery and should have been made in the last five years. Accepted work is delivered at the artist's expense: shipped pieces must arrive by 19 February 2027 with a prepaid return label and a reusable container, or be hand-delivered on 21 or 23 February, and picked up on 12 April. Wall-hung work is capped at 50 lbs and free-standing work at 300 lbs, with a maximum width of 64 inches for a 10-foot wall. Selected work must stay up for the whole run, and anything left 30 days after the close becomes SebArts property. — Deadline: January 6, 2027. Fee: $35 (2 images), $10 each additional. Prize: $300 / $200 / $100 + two $50 coordinator awards + Group exhibition.

item.title: ARC + ATHENA Artist Residency 2027 · ARC Gallery
item.description:
A new ten-month remote residency from A.R.C. Gallery, the artist-run Chicago cooperative founded in 1973, funded by its philanthropic partner ATHENA and administered by the ARC Gallery & Educational Foundation. Three artists are selected each year from an international pool and work as a cohort, developing individual bodies of work while meeting weekly online with each other and monthly with ARC member mentors, alongside professional development sessions on exhibition preparation, documentation, writing, networking and career sustainability, and introductions to visiting curators and arts professionals.
The 2027 cycle runs February to November 2027 and culminates in three concurrent solo exhibitions at ARC Gallery in Chicago in November 2027. Residents work from their own studios - relocation is not required - but should plan to travel to Chicago for installation and the opening, and travel costs are not covered. Each resident receives $1,500 through ATHENA: a $1,200 artist stipend plus a $300 shipping allowance that may instead go toward materials. ARC takes no commission, so 100% of any sale price goes to the artist, and installation, de-installation, press, social media and a first-Friday opening reception are handled by ARC members. The residency includes a community-engagement element - a demonstration or workshop - and the application asks what you would like it to be.
The call is open to artists working in any medium at any education level, with no stated geographic or age bar, though the CV you paste into the form should demonstrate at least four years of serious pursuit of a career in art. The application takes 10 images (JPG/JPEG; video work as a still plus a clip of up to two minutes in MP4/MOV), an artist statement of no more than 125 words, a two-page CV, two professional references and written answers on process, workspace and internet reliability, collaboration, what you hope to explore, and why ARC. Images are uploaded to Dropbox before the form is paid for. Applications close 15 December 2026 at 11:59 pm CST; review is in January and notification in early February 2027. Entry is $40, and ARC states that limited fee waivers are available on request by email before submitting. — Deadline: December 15, 2026. Fee: $40 (waivers available). Prize: Ten-month residency + solo exhibition + $1,500.

item.title: The Petrides Residency for a Greek Artist in NY · New York Foundation for the Arts
item.description:
A fully funded three-month residency in New York for one artist based in Greece, newly established by the Athens- and New York-based sculptor George Petrides with the International Studio & Curatorial Program (ISCP) in Brooklyn and administered by NYFA. Photography is one of seven named eligible disciplines, alongside craft/sculpture, digital/electronic arts, interdisciplinary work, painting, printmaking/drawing/book arts and video/film.
The inaugural residency runs 1 October to 31 December 2027 at ISCP, 1040 Metropolitan Avenue, Brooklyn. The selected artist receives 24/7 access to a private furnished studio of 334 square feet, a monthly stipend of $3,000 for accommodation, living expenses and materials ($9,000 across the three months), and a one-time payment of $1,000 toward airfare and local travel. The programme includes at least one hour-long meeting a month with visiting critics, field trips, gallery walks and Fall Open Studios, and the option to join NYFA's professional development programmes. The artist arranges their own travel and housing; ISCP expects roughly 20 studio hours a week.
To apply you must be a practising artist in one or more of the eligible disciplines, hold a valid Greek passport, be a current full-time resident of Greece and have been for at least two years at the time applications opened, be 30 or older by 20 October 2026, have working English, and not be enrolled in a full-time degree programme. Artist duos of two may apply together on one shared stipend and studio. Proof of residency and age is required of the selected artist.
The application asks for a CV or bio of up to five pages, up to 10 images (or a mix of 5 images and one audio/video link), a 150-word work-sample note and three 250-word statements on the proposed project, the practice and why New York. An independent three-person panel scores applications, shortlists three finalists for virtual interviews and makes the final choice; all applicants hear in February 2027 and the recipient is announced publicly in March. Applications must be in English and go through Submittable; there is no application fee. — Deadline: December 8, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $9,000 stipend + Residency.

item.title: Rauschenberg Medical Emergency Grants - Cycle 39 · New York Foundation for the Arts
item.description:
One-time grants of up to $5,000 for recent unexpected medical, dental and mental-health emergencies, funded by the Robert Rauschenberg Foundation and administered by NYFA. The eligible Visual Arts category names Photography outright - 'work in traditional and experimental photography or any work in which photography or photographic techniques are pivotal, if not exclusive' - alongside craft/sculpture, painting and printmaking/drawing/book arts, and the programme also covers digital/electronic arts, video/film and choreography.
Applicants must be 21 or older, reside in the United States, the District of Columbia, a Tribal Nation or a U.S. Territory, and meet the income cap: adjusted gross income no greater than $80,000 for an individual or $160,000 for joint filers, averaged over the last two federal tax returns. You also need recent and sustained artistic activity - at least one public-facing opportunity a year since 2022 - and you cannot be enrolled in any degree-seeking programme or have received a Rauschenberg Medical or Dancer Emergency Grant within the last five years.
Cycle 39 covers emergencies occurring on or after 1 April 2026. Applications opened 20 October and close at 5:00 PM ET on 17 November 2026, with notification on 23 December 2026. Treatment is only covered if it took place in the U.S., D.C., a Tribal Nation or a U.S. Territory. Artists whose direct medical costs are covered by Medicare or Medicaid may instead request up to $5,000 in documented living expenses. Portfolios and work samples are not requested - applications are reviewed for demonstrated need - but your CV must show five years of practice. Roughly $138,000 is distributed each cycle and demand outstrips it, so applying is not a guarantee of an award. Awarding is a two-step process: NYFA staff screen for eligibility, an outside panel then scores on demonstrated need and severity, and after that review the top-scoring application is funded automatically while the rest of the top tier go into a lottery for the remaining awards. Cycle 40 opens 15 December 2026 and closes 12 January 2027. — Deadline: November 17, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Up to $5,000.

item.title: MUSE Photography Awards 2027 · International Awards Associate
item.description:
The 2027 MUSE Photography Awards are open. International Awards Associate — the group behind several geographically titled photography and design competitions — runs the awards across 12 main categories (Advertising, Architecture, Black & White, Commercial, Editorial, Fashion, Film, Fine Art, Minimalist, Nature, People and a Special Category) subdivided into 345 subcategories, with separate Professional and Amateur/Student divisions carrying the same categories.
Entry closes in four stages: early bird 16 October to 19 November 2026, regular 20 November to 17 December 2026, final 18 December 2026 to 14 January 2027, and a final extension 15 January to 25 February 2027. Each stage costs more than the last. A professional single image runs $30 early bird to $45 at final extension and a professional series of two to eight images $40 to $55; an amateur or student single runs $25 to $40 and an amateur or student series $35 to $50. Additional categories are $20 to $35, and a Multi Entry Pass is $185 for ten credits, one credit per category entry.
Photographer of the Year takes $3,000 in the Professional division and $2,000 in Amateur/Student, with the MUSE statuette; Category Winner of the Year takes $100. The Platinum, Gold and Silver tiers below that are scored bands (85–100, 75–84, 65–74) on the jury's 1–100 scale and carry no cash — winners receive winner pages, interviews, e-certificates and badges, and may buy a personalised statuette. Cash prizes do not stack, so each winner receives only the highest one they qualify for. Results are announced on 16 April 2027.
The competition is open to entrants aged 18 and over worldwide, professional, amateur and student alike. Entry is a single image or a series of two to eight images; work must have been made within the last five years (2023–2027), and previously published or previously awarded photographs are allowed. Judging is blind. Entering means creating an account on the awards site. The Special Category carries a dedicated AI-Generated Photography subcategory (SP2701); no surface we could read states a policy on AI use in the other eleven categories. — Deadline: February 25, 2027. Fee: $25–$55. Prize: $3,000.

item.title: Open Call for Exhibition Proposals 2027–2029 · Second Street Gallery
item.description:
Second Street Gallery — founded in 1973 and the oldest nonprofit contemporary art space in Central Virginia, mounting 10 to 14 exhibitions a year — is taking proposals for its Main Gallery and smaller Dové Gallery for the seasons running October 2027 to January 2029.
This is a rolling call. Proposals are read periodically by the gallery's Executive Director and Chief Curator, Kristen Chiacchia, as the calendar fills, and the call closes once every slot is taken; the gallery says applying early matters because fewer dates remain as the calendar is built. Individual artists, collaborating artists and curators can all apply, for solo, two-person or group exhibitions. There is no geographic restriction and artists at every career stage are invited, though full-time students can only be included in group shows. Applicants choose which gallery they want to be considered for and which of five exhibition windows they are free for. Artwork should generally have been made within five years of the exhibition date unless the proposal is a retrospective or has a clear curatorial reason for earlier work.
An application takes 7 to 15 images, an image list, a proposal, an artist or curatorial statement, CV, an estimate of scope, installation requirements, and a sketch of one or more public programmes — an artist talk, workshop, screening, tour or whatever suits the practice — which the gallery develops with the artist and pays for separately, with programme honoraria starting at $100.
Selected exhibitions receive a $1,000 honorarium towards production, packing, shipping, travel and lodging; for two-person and group shows that sum is per exhibition, split as agreed. Artists arrange and pay for transport of the work. At least 75% of the work shown must be for sale, with exemptions possible for installation, video, performance, site-specific and time-based work, and the gallery takes 50% commission on sales. If selected, artists must attend the opening in Charlottesville and take part in at least one public programme.
Work created or substantially generated with generative AI is not accepted. Entry is $35, or $20 for current gallery members. — Deadline: November 1, 2027. Fee: $35 ($20 members). Prize: $1,000 honorarium + Exhibition.

item.title: Mind to Medium · Artspiration Frederick
item.description:
Artspiration Frederick, a nonprofit arts organisation in Frederick, Maryland, is running Mind to Medium, a juried exhibition about the journey from thought to expression — "from the first spark of an idea to its realization through materials and techniques", and how artists turn the intangible into something you can stand in front of.
All media are accepted, and photography is named explicitly alongside painting, drawing, printmaking, sculpture, fibre art, ceramics, mixed media and digital art. Artists living in the continental United States, aged 18 and over, can submit up to three works, all three of which may be selected; work must not have been shown at Artspiration Frederick before and must be for sale, with prices fixed at application. Two-dimensional work has to be framed and wired — no sawtooth hangers — and a 300 dpi image is needed for the jury.
The juror is S. Manya Stoumen-Tolino, a contemporary expressionist painter based in New Market, Maryland, with a BFA from the Philadelphia College of Art and an MFA from the University of Pennsylvania. Notifications go out by 18 February 2027. The show runs 5 to 27 March 2027 at the organisation's gallery at 915 Toll House Avenue, with an opening reception on 13 March, 3 to 5pm; the gallery is free to enter and wheelchair accessible.
Work is dropped off 28 February and 1–2 March, or shipped to arrive by 3 March with return postage included. The gallery takes 40% commission on sales, with 60% to the artist. Entry is $35, or $25 for members. — Deadline: February 12, 2027. Fee: $35 ($25 members). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Paper · NEXT Gallery
item.description:
NEXT Gallery, “owned and operated by 28 working artists” and sitting in the 40 West Arts Hub in Lakewood, Colorado, has an open call "for anything made of or on paper". The gallery is looking for paper treated as a creative medium in its own right — inks, graphite, paints, mark-making, cutting, manipulating, casting, creasing, sculpting and fashioning — and says traditional and unconventional approaches are equally welcome.
All media are accepted except AI art. Work has to be finished, in good condition and ready to hang without sawtooth hangers, smaller than five feet in any one dimension, with shipped pieces capped at 36 inches for safe handling; exceptions depend on the piece and the space available. Three-dimensional artists are asked to submit a video of the work. Up to three entries can be submitted for a single $35 fee.
The juror is Karen Eberle-Smith, a Denver artist who works mainly with handmade paper on themes of fragility and resilience, has shown at the Depot Art Gallery and Denver Botanic Gardens, and has been a NEXT Gallery member since 2023. Artists are notified by Friday 26 March 2027.
The exhibition runs 16 April to 2 May 2027, with the opening reception on 16 April. Accepted work is dropped off on 11 and 12 April, or mailed to arrive by 10 April with prepaid return shipping included — work without it will not be hung. The gallery takes 33% commission on sales and pays out within a month of the show closing. — Deadline: March 15, 2027. Fee: $35. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: THE BLACK EXPERIENCE · Tall Grass Arts Association
item.description:
Tall Grass Arts Association, a seventy-year-old non-profit gallery in Park Forest, Illinois that keeps its exhibitions free to the public, opens its 2027 season with THE BLACK EXPERIENCE, a Black History Month exhibition for African American artists. The brief is wide and deliberately personal: works may share images or interpretations of the artists’ own lives, experiences, lessons, influences, challenges, fears, struggles and victories. The gallery asks artists to consider negative and positive events and the quality of daily life, injustices and rewards, decisions made and the people who inspired them, histories of lost hope and long-held dreams for the future; images of people who made a difference, texts of important speeches or writings, situations of changing conditions and the struggles to make those changes; and works that refer to events, relationships, talents and other art forms that educate, document or inspire.
Photographers are squarely inside this one — photography and digital works are named in the accepted-media list alongside painting, drawing, printmaking, graphic design, mixed media and collage, calligraphy, books, sculpture, fibre, glass, ceramics and metal, and any medium except video is acceptable in all sizes, styles and formats. Selection is by a named panel: curators Claudia Craemer and Deb Craemer, joined for the choice of works by photographer Perry Slade and painter Eurnice Harris. They weigh the traditional criteria — compositional elements, use of media, technical skill — together with each artist’s own vision and the impact and lasting impression of the piece, and say that for this show in particular the power of a work’s message will also count.
Up to five works per artist, submitted through EntryThingy. The prospectus itself prints no price: EntryThingy’s record for the call carries a single $25 entry fee and publishes no per-work ladder above it, so treat $25 as a floor until the entry form shows a total — it can be paid on EntryThingy, by card over the phone, or in person at the gallery in cash, by check or by card. Note what this show does not offer: works will not be judged for awards, though visitors’ votes are collected for the most outstanding pieces. Shipped work is accepted if the artist supplies a pre-paid return shipping label; two-dimensional work must be wired and ready to hang, with no sawtooth hangers and no wires showing above the frame, and anything needing special installation must be installed by the artist. All work stays up for the full run. Artists are notified by 8 December 2026, required forms are due by 18 December, work is delivered to the gallery on 3–6 January 2027, the exhibition runs 16 January – 19 February 2027, and work is returned 20–23 February. Unless an artist asks otherwise, Tall Grass takes permission to use images of exhibited work for publicity or educational purposes. — Deadline: November 28, 2026. Fee: From $25. Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: 215 Magill Residency 2027 · Helpmann Academy
item.description:
Helpmann Academy's 215 Magill Residency gives one emerging South Australian visual artist or designer a dedicated studio for twelve months at 215 Magill, a design studio and workshop in Maylands, Adelaide, where a community of practising artists and makers works in furniture, art and design. The residency is valued at A$6,000 in kind rather than paid as a fee: an allocated studio space from 1 February 2027 to 31 January 2028, 24-hour access with security and WIFI, access to and training on a full machine shop for woodwork, use of a ceramics kiln, and mentoring from 215 Magill founder Mark Jones. It ends in a group exhibition with the other artists-in-residence at the fab workshop and studios, held at St Peters Town Hall Gallery as part of Adelaide Fringe in February–March 2028.
Photographers are inside this one even though the workshop's own tools lean towards timber and clay: Photography is one of the artform specialisations the application form itself offers under Visual Arts, alongside painting, sculpture, ceramics, installation, moving image, print making and new media. What narrows the door is not medium but geography and career stage. Applications are invited from graduates with a practice in visual arts holding a supported degree from Adelaide University, Flinders University, the University of South Australia or the University of Adelaide, up to seven years from graduation. Honours students and graduates qualify where honours followed directly on from the undergraduate degree; Masters and PhD graduates and candidates are not eligible unless they still qualify through an undergraduate or honours degree. Anyone with an overdue acquittal on a previous Helpmann award is ineligible. Two Helpmann surfaces disagree on how long the door stays open: this residency's own Information for Applicants page says seven years from graduation, while the academy's general Who We Support page allows five years measured from 31 December of the final year of study and lists only two other programmes as seven-year exceptions. The eligible degrees are closed dropdown lists on the form, so anyone near the edge of either window, or whose course name is not listed, should ask the academy to confirm eligibility before writing — both pages invite exactly that.
Applying is free, but the required material takes time to assemble: three written responses of up to 500 words each, an artist CV of no more than two pages, an official academic transcript showing the conferral date, a letter of support on letterhead from a current or former lecturer or from an industry professional who can speak to the practice — uploaded with the form, never sent separately — and up to five images and/or audio-visual demos, each file no larger than 10MB and no more than 50MB in total. Reviews or press coverage of past work, extra support letters and further audio-visual material are optional additions. Applications opened at noon ACDT on Tuesday 13 October 2026 and close at 11:59 pm ACDT on Tuesday 24 November 2026. An optional studio tour on Wednesday 28 October 2026 lets applicants meet 2026 resident Chelsie Morey and Mark Jones and see the machinery and spaces before they write, and Helpmann's programme manager is available to discuss an application online or in person before submission. An unnamed panel assesses every application on artistic merit, the impact of the residency on practice and career growth, the vision for the equipment and the creative community, and readiness to take it on; shortlisted applicants may be interviewed and the panel's decisions are final. The recipient commits to at least 20 hours a week in the studio, holds public liability insurance for the duration, supplies images and content for Helpmann's social channels, and credits the academy in publicity for the work it supports. — Deadline: November 24, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: 12-month studio + Fringe exhibition.

item.title: Project Grants: Art Activities in Public Spaces 2027–2028 · Indy Arts Council
item.description:
The Indy Arts Council's project grants fund arts activities that happen in public space in Marion County, Indiana — parks, libraries and comparable sites — with awards between $2,000 and $10,000 and no match requirement. The grant period runs from 1 April 2027 to 31 March 2028, and all activity must start and finish inside it. The council says a limited pool is available and that projects at Indy Parks or Indianapolis Public Library sites may be prioritised where they align with that site's own goals.
Individual artists may apply alongside nonprofits, which is what makes this one worth a photographer's attention: an artist applicant needs only to be 18 or over, a resident of Marion County, and able to give a Social Security Number, ITIN or A-Number. One application per applicant, one project per application. The eligible disciplines named in the guidelines include visual arts and media arts, and the kinds of activity named are festivals, performances, workshops and programming — so a community darkroom series, a temporary photographic installation in a park, or a public photo-walk programme all fit, while permanent public art installations are explicitly excluded. Anyone awarded an Indy Arts Council project grant in either of the last two rounds (since November 2025) is barred from this one, as are schools, universities, booster clubs, friends groups and fundraising-only organisations. All programme-related expenses are eligible for funding, including artist fees.
The written application is submitted free through the council's grant platform by 11:59 pm on Sunday 10 January 2027; alternate formats (dictated or video responses, other languages) are offered on request to the grants office. Applications are reviewed through January and February, with award notifications in early March 2027 and a final report due 30 April 2028. Final determinations are made by the council with a group of outside reviewers that includes local artists and staff from Indy Parks and the Indianapolis Public Library. Two optional call-out meetings were held in October 2026 and the Zoom session is posted as a recording. The programme is funded by the City of Indianapolis, the Capital Improvement Board, the Indianapolis Local Improvement Bond Bank, Glick Philanthropies and the Allen Whitehill Clowes Charitable Foundation. — Deadline: January 10, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: $2,000–$10,000.

item.title: Blog & Substack Interview Open Call · Photo Trouvée Magazine
item.description:
Photo Trouvée Magazine — a small independent publication built around vintage found and family photographs — runs a rolling open call for artists to be featured in a written interview on its website blog and its Substack. The invitation is to artists working with or inspired by vintage found or family photographs, in any media and at any stage of their career, and it is open internationally.
The interview is a question-and-answer feature rather than a portfolio spread. The application form publishes the whole question bank — fifteen prompts covering how the artist began working with vintage photographs, process, themes, current inspirations, the relationship between found photographs and family archives, advice for emerging artists working in the medium, dream projects, studio time around jobs and parenting, how the artist archives their own collection of vintage photographs, and admired vintage-photo artists — and asks each applicant to answer only five to seven of them. Applicants also upload six to ten images: work, studio shots, exhibition shots, headshots or anything else that would sit well alongside the text. The magazine asks for well-lit, well-cropped files named First_Last_Title.
There is no deadline: submissions are accepted on a rolling basis and the magazine releases selected interviews over the following months, notifying each artist by email when theirs goes live. The editors describe themselves as a team of two and ask for patience on timing. The fee is $15, paid through the form, and the magazine says fees support its work and a scholarship fund for its own programmes; they are non-refundable. Selection is not guaranteed by submitting. The magazine's audience sits in the found-photography niche — it reports a social following above 23,000 and its print issues are carried at Kobby Gallery in São Paulo and the Coral Springs Museum of Art shop in Florida. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: $15. Prize: Publication (online interview).

item.title: Interlace Emergency Grants
item.description:
Interlace Emergency Grants are small, fast grants for Providence-area visual artists facing an emergency — the fund names eviction, a utility shut-off, healthcare expenses and a phone or internet cut-off among the situations it exists for. Awards run from $50 to $500 out of a pool of $1,250 dispersed every month; if a month's qualified requests come to less than the pool, the remainder rolls forward.
The programme never closes, but it runs on a published monthly cycle rather than one competition: applications are due on the 7th of each month, applicants are notified by the 21st, and funds are disbursed in the final week. Artists may apply as often as they need within a calendar year up to a $500 ceiling, so a photographer who received $100 one month can come back for the rest, and an unsuccessful applicant may simply reapply. Applications go through Submittable, which requires a free account that Interlace says it uses to protect applicants' privacy; they are anonymised by Interlace staff before review and read by an independent group of local arts, education and community-service professionals. Recipients are not publicly announced, and the money is unrestricted with no reporting requirements.
To be eligible an applicant must self-identify as a visual artist, be over 18 at the time of applying, have lived in Rhode Island for at least a year within a 10-mile radius of the City of Providence (the fund is explicit that the radius does not extend into Massachusetts), and not be a full-time student or enrolled in a degree programme. Emergency Grant applicants do not need to be US citizens. Interlace publishes its whole question set as a downloadable PDF: the application asks for a description of the emergency in up to 300 words (or a two-minute audio or video recording instead), the amount requested, a work sample of three to five images or a CV, resume or short video — or a portfolio link in place of files — and, separately, a link to an artist website, a public social account with a reasonable history of current work or an article verifying the practice; those who can supply neither are invited to get in touch instead. An applicant must also be able to receive a cheque in their legal name, and anyone employed by or related to the partnering institutions' staff, residents or board is barred. The fund asks applicants to use the honour system and apply only where livelihood or well-being is genuinely affected. Interlace is backed by the Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts and partners in Providence. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: Free. Prize: $50–$500.

item.title: Main Gallery Exhibition Submissions · Blue Sky Gallery
item.description:
Blue Sky, the Oregon Center for the Photographic Arts, accepts proposals for its main gallery year-round. The Portland non-profit has shown photography since 1975 and is currently scheduling new exhibition selections for late 2027 and beyond, so a proposal sent now is read against that calendar rather than a single themed show.
The Exhibition Committee reviews every submission equally and takes work from emerging, mid-career and established artists; Blue Sky membership is not a prerequisite for consideration. The gallery states plainly that it receives hundreds of submissions each year, cannot respond to status enquiries and does not give feedback on work it turns down; it asks for up to six months to reply. An automatic email confirms that a submission arrived, and the gallery asks anyone who does not get one to submit again.
All work must be photo- or video-based. A submission is 15 to 30 images from a single body of work, formatted as one horizontal 8.5 x 11 inch PDF (one image per page, black background, no borders, no watermarks) or a zip of individual JPGs, with the whole upload kept under 10 MB; video goes in as a zip or as a PDF carrying a viewing link. A concise artist statement and a CV go with it. Separate bodies of work are submitted individually, and the gallery asks explicitly that nothing be sent by post or email — only through the form on its submissions page. There is no submission fee. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: Free. Prize: Gallery exhibition in Portland.

item.title: Catalyst Artist Development Programme · Photoworks (with Pompey Darkroom)
item.description:
Catalyst is a new artist development programme run jointly by Photoworks and Pompey Darkroom, bringing together eight photographers for five months of masterclasses, peer learning and one-to-one mentoring between November 2026 and March 2027. It is part of Photography Champions, the national initiative Photoworks leads with public funding through Arts Council England's National Portfolio.
The masterclass line-up is named on the call page: Jermaine Francis on presenting work and expanded photography, Amak Mahmoodian on research and approaches to making, Gordon MacDonald on bookmaking, Danit Ariel on curating, and Alejandra Carles-Tolra on facilitation as practice. Alongside the sessions, each participant gets individual mentoring shaped around their own practice, and the group is given a dedicated budget to decide together how to present the work made during the programme — an exhibition, a public event or a photobook.
The call is open to UK-based emerging photographers, with applications particularly welcomed from photographers in Portsmouth and the wider South. Sessions mix online and in-person meetings, including weekday evenings and weekends. Applying is free, and the whole application goes as one PDF — a CV, a maximum 400-word statement on why you are applying and how the programme would help, links to your website and social media, and a selection of your images — to the darkroom's submissions@ inbox with 'Catalyst' as the subject line. Taking part is not free — the programme fee is £200, payable in full or in two instalments (November and February), and two fully-funded bursary places are available for Portsmouth-based photographers who cannot afford it; applicants ask to be considered for one in the application itself. Applications close on 30 October 2026 and the first session is on 2 November. — Deadline: October 30, 2026. Fee: Free (£200 programme fee if selected). Prize: None listed.

item.title: Open Call Rotterdam 2027 · Hungry Eye Fair
item.description:
Hungry Eye Fair — the Rotterdam photography fair founded in 2015 as Haute Photographie — opens its twelfth edition to independent photographers. The 2027 Rotterdam edition runs 17–21 March, and the open call is the route for photographers outside the fair's invited roster to show work alongside the established names it exhibits.
The call is open to all photographers regardless of where they live. Applicants send a résumé and a portfolio as a PDF (the fair explicitly refuses WeTransfer links) to the fair's own submissions inbox, with the subject line the page's apply button fills in. The deadline is 1 November 2026.
Applying is free. The fair states plainly that taking part is not: "Applying for the open call is free, but participation at Hungry Eye Fair requires a contribution." No amount is published anywhere on the call page, so selected photographers should ask what the contribution is before committing. — Deadline: November 1, 2026. Fee: Free (contribution if selected). Prize: Exhibition at the fair.

item.title: Portfolio Reviews Equity Scholarships 2027 · Colorado Photographic Arts Center
item.description:
The Month of Photography Denver Festival portfolio reviews are the largest professional review event in the Rocky Mountain region: over two days, 30 gallery owners, curators and publishers meet 70 artists at The Slate Hotel on 12–13 March 2027. CPAC grants a limited number of scholarships so that photographers who have historically had less access to those rooms can take part.
Each scholarship recipient receives eight portfolio review sessions, two nights at The Slate Hotel, support for travel to and from the event, an hour-long preparation meeting with CPAC Executive Director and Curator Samantha Johnston, inclusion in the Photography Showcase & Book Fair at The Studio Loft in the Ellie Caulkins Opera House, and a one-year individual CPAC membership.
Applicants must be 18 or over and lens-based artists who identify as BIPOC and/or LGBTQIA2S+ and/or have a disability. Applicants may live anywhere in the United States, with preference given to artists who live and work in Colorado. The application is a JotForm asking for ten photographs, a one-page biographical statement as a PDF or Word document, and a CV as a PDF. Applications are open from 11 September to 3 November 2026, and awards are announced on 16 December 2026. — Deadline: November 3, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Portfolio review fellowship.

item.title: First Look 2027 · Panopticon Gallery
item.description:
Panopticon Gallery's annual juried portfolio exhibition, on view in its Boston gallery from February to April 2027. Photographers submit up to ten images from a single cohesive body of work; roughly five images from each selected portfolio go into the show. The gallery frames the call as a way for its curatorial team to find new voices, and says submissions are also considered for future group and solo exhibitions.
Every submitted portfolio is additionally considered for First Look: A Second Glance, a companion exhibition of single images that runs alongside the main show on The Wall at Panopticon Gallery. Prints shown there afterwards enter the gallery's flat files, where they stay available to collectors and gallery patrons.
Submission runs through a Google Form: up to ten JPEGs (sRGB, 1000–1500 px on the long side, named LastName_FirstName_Title.jpg), an artist or project statement, and a link to a website or social media. The fee is $40 per portfolio, or $30 for students with a valid student ID, and must be paid for the work to be juried. Accepted work has to reach the gallery by 4 February 2027, with most pieces framed to about 20 x 24 inches; the gallery takes a 50% commission on sales, and selected artists get 20% off printing and framing at Panopticon Imaging, which also delivers to the gallery. The show opens 11 February and closes 29 April 2027. — Deadline: December 29, 2026. Fee: $40 / $30 student. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: New York Open Call 2027 · Arrival Gallery
item.description:
Arrival Gallery runs three-day group shows in a rotating list of cities. Its pages name London, Lisbon, Athens, Brighton, Madrid, Manila, Osaka and Milan as well as New York. This call is for a show at 35 Meadow Street, Brooklyn, from 12 to 14 March 2027. It has an open theme and is open to all visual media, including fine-art, documentary, portrait, street and experimental photography, with work shown either physically or on screens.
Submitting is free, but the show is paid for by the artists who are selected. Arrival's open-calls page says selected artists pay a participation fee covering the venue and promotion, starting from £50. The New York page does not give the amount: the fee, format and preparation details are sent only after selection, before the artist confirms a place. For comparison, Arrival's current London call prices places from £65 (digital) and £165 (physical).
Applying starts with a mailing-list signup. The application link asks for an email address and sends a Typeform link to it, and signing up also adds you to Arrival's mailing list. The application asks for images, an artist statement and details of your practice. Selected artists get a place in the show, a profile on Arrival's website and social channels where applicable, and sales support where the format allows. — Deadline: February 25, 2027. Fee: Free (participation fee if selected, amount not published). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: London Artist Showcase · Arrival Gallery
item.description:
