Arrival Gallery runs three-day group shows in a rotating list of cities, and this call is for its London show at 56 Dawes Road, Fulham, from 13 to 15 November 2026. It has an open theme and is open to all visual media, including fine-art, documentary, portrait, street and experimental photography.
Submitting is free, but the show is paid for by the artists who are selected. The London page sells three routes: a Digital Showcase from £65, where the work is shown on screens without shipping anything; a Physical Showcase from £165, with the work hung in the space; and a limited Featured place with extra promotion, whose price is not published. When read on 24 October the page listed 40 digital, 40 physical and 5 featured places as available in the current batch. The exact fee, format and timeline are sent after selection, before the artist confirms a place. Physical work has to be delivered or shipped by the artist.
Applying starts with a mailing-list signup. The application link asks for a name and email address, with a marketing-email consent box, and sends a Typeform link to that address. Selected artists get a place in the show, preparation guidance and promotion through Arrival's channels, and may be considered for its other cities. — Deadline: November 1, 2026. Fee: Free (£65+ digital, £165+ physical if selected). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Call for Exhibitions — Spring 2028 · Photographic Gallery Hippolyte
item.description: Photographic Gallery Hippolyte in Helsinki, run by the Association of Photographic Artists, is taking applications for its Spring 2028 exhibition season. The call is open to all forms of contemporary art, but photography carries the programme: proposals are expected to connect to photographic art or the extended field of photography more than superficially, and the application text must spell that connection out when it is not obvious. Professional practitioners, artists, artist groups and curators may all apply with a ready-made exhibition concept, and the gallery states plainly that applicants need not be based in Finland or be members of the association, and that it welcomes both artists at the start of a career and long-established ones. There are two spaces - the gallery itself at about 72 square metres and Hippolyte Studio at about 13 - and one application may request the gallery, the studio or the whole space. Exhibition slots run January to June 2028 and last about five weeks including installation, deinstallation and opening. Applying is free, and since 2025 the exhibition space has been rent-free for every artist, with the association also paying an exhibition fee; it is explicit that rent-free status is decided annually on funding, and that the maximum rents that would otherwise apply are 650 euro for the gallery, 280 for the studio and 930 for both for association members, and 1,000, 280 and 1,280 for non-members. Rent, when charged, covers invigilation, visitor tracking, staff support with planning and installation, the opening reception, documentation, press and publicity. The exhibitor installs the work and pays for transport, insurance, travel and any AV equipment, which the gallery does not own, and the association takes a 30 percent commission on works and associated material sold, with selected works also carried in its online shop for up to three months after the show. Applications go through an online form linked from the gallery's Apply for an exhibition page, as a single PDF of no more than ten pages and 5 MB holding a one-page exhibition plan, up to ten supporting images and a condensed CV; each applicant can submit only once, nothing is accepted by email or post, and late applications are not considered. A three-to-five-member exhibition committee drawn from the association, plus two visiting assessors including one expert from outside it, peer-review every application, and all applicants hear personally, by email or text message, before Midsummer. The gallery hopes to programme work not previously shown in the Helsinki metropolitan area, and a selected artist agrees to hold no solo show of the same content there in the twelve months before the exhibition or during it. An artist may be granted a new Hippolyte slot once five years have passed since their previous one. The call opens twice a year, in April and October, about eighteen months ahead of the season; this round runs 1-31 October 2026, and the gallery receives around 250 applications a year. — Deadline: October 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition + artist fee.

item.title: By Degrees · Bitfactory Gallery
item.description: National juried exhibition at Bitfactory Gallery & Studios, an artist-run gallery and studio building in Denver, on the theme By Degrees: 'Same coordinates. Different point of view.' The call asks artists to consider the subtle movements in attention and significance that accumulate while we appear to stand still - what once filled the frame becoming one detail among many or slipping past the edge, an ordinary moment turning absorbing, a quiet one feeling unexpectedly full - and says the theme is a point of departure with room for ambiguity, discovery and individual interpretation. Open to artists aged 18 and over resident in the United States, working in all media; work must be original, must not have been shown at Bitfactory before, must be available for sale and may be no larger than 48 by 48 inches excluding the frame. The juror is Brayden Espinosa, a working artist and the gallery manager at Bitfactory Gallery & Studios and Block Gallery in Denver. Entry is through CaFE: the checkout charges $35 for the first image plus $5 for each additional image, to a maximum of ten. CAUTION: the gallery's own page prints a different entry fee, "$25 for three images", while the CaFE record that takes the payment charges $35 for one image and repeats that figure in its fee block, its requirements text and its listing; budget for the CaFE figure. Notification by 2 December; shipped work must arrive by 13 December and hand-delivered work on 14 December; the show opens with a reception on 18 December 2026 and closes 9 January 2027. Two terms worth weighing before entering: the gallery retains a 50 percent commission on sales, and artists pay insurance and shipping both ways, including a prepaid return label. Hand-delivered work left more than two days after the close accrues a $10 per day storage fee. — Deadline: December 1, 2026. Fee: $35 for 1 image, $5 each additional. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Embracing Our Differences 2028 Outdoor Exhibition
item.description: International outdoor juried exhibition, running annually since 2004. Fifty selected artworks are reproduced as billboard-size panels — 16 feet (4.88 m) wide by 12.5 feet (3.81 m) high — each paired with a quotation, and displayed from mid-January to April 2028 in Sarasota and St. Petersburg, Florida. Three cash awards of $2,000 each: Best-in-Show Adult, Best-in-Show Student and People's Choice, the last voted by exhibition visitors. Work must reflect the theme Embracing Our Differences — inclusivity, freedom of expression, individuality, resilience in the face of bullying, discrimination or societal barriers, and building bridges between groups. Artwork may be created in any size or medium: the guidelines name no medium and exclude none, and one judging criterion rewards work that adds to the variety of media in the final selection, so photography competes on the same terms as any other medium. The file must be horizontal at a 16:11 aspect ratio, at least 300 dpi at 12.8 by 8.8 inches (3840 × 2640 pixels or larger recommended, 600 dpi preferred) and under 400 MB, in JPG, PDF or PNG. A 150-word artist statement is required; the guidelines cap titles at five words in one line and at "less than 5 words" in another, so four words is the safe maximum. Entry is free with no limit on the number of submissions, each submitted as a separate entry — online through Zealous, or by post with a signed form, colour print and statement per artwork. Open worldwide to professional, emerging, student and amateur artists; online entrants must be 13 or over, younger artists with a parent or guardian's consent. Selection is by a blind judging panel of professional artists, curators and art professionals, judging in early fall 2027; only artists whose work is selected are notified individually, by email, and all winning entries are posted on the organisation's website by early January. AI-generated artwork is not accepted and may be disqualified; the organisers may ask for a process description or work-in-progress images. Artists keep ownership of their work and grant the organisation a non-exclusive worldwide licence for exhibition and promotional use. — Deadline: July 1, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: $2,000 × 3.

item.title: Under My Skin Issue #3 — With Us (ARE YOU?) · California Aggregation for Gender Diversity
item.description: Third issue of Under My Skin, the magazine published by the California Aggregation for Gender Diversity, a nonprofit building community, resources and public education around Transgender, Genderqueer, Intersex and Nonbinary (TGIN+) topics through history and art programming. Where the first two issues, Shadows and Euphoria, explored different parts of the self, issue 3 turns to the collective feelings of the gender diverse community and asks who is truly With Us: what being With Us looks like, how it feels when the people who say they love you vote for your demise, how politics isolate — and, on the other side, how people who will stand up for you are found. Photography and all other forms of visual art are welcome alongside poems, essays and articles; music and film can be promoted even though they cannot be printed on paper. Submissions are especially encouraged from artists who are multiply marginalised, chronically ill, disabled, trans, intersex, undocumented, incarcerated or formerly incarcerated, low-income and otherwise systemically excluded, and contributors may use a pseudonym. Contributors receive a digital copy of the published issue, credit lines and artwork descriptions alongside their images, and promotion through the organisation's website and social channels. The issue publishes December 1, 2026. — Deadline: November 8, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication + digital copy.

item.title: Epson International Pano Awards 2027
item.description: 18th edition of the world's largest international competition dedicated to panoramic photography, entries now open. Three divisions run in parallel: Open Awards (open to all photographers, US$22 per image), Amateur Awards (US$20 per image, restricted to photographers earning less than US$20,000 a year from photography) and VR/360 Awards (US$20 per image). Open and Amateur each take Nature/Landscapes, Aerial and Built Environment categories; VR/360 runs as a single category. A panorama is defined as a minimum 2:1 aspect ratio on the long side, and entries may be stitched and/or cropped from multiple or single captures, at any focal length. Open and Amateur files must be exactly 3000 pixels on the long side and no more than 1500 on the short side; VR/360 files exactly 6144 × 3072 pixels. There is no age limit and no cap on entries, but images already shortlisted (top 10 in any category) or given a major or special award in a previous Pano Awards may not be re-entered. Entering five or more images at once takes 20% off the total entry fee — note that these multiple-entry discounts are withdrawn in the final entry period, which follows the June 21, 2027 early-bird close and runs to the July 12 deadline; the per-image fee itself does not rise. Early-bird entrants who also score in the top 50 of Open or Amateur, or the top 20 in VR/360, are in the running for the US$1,000 Curator's Award, chosen by curator David Evans. At least three images in Open or Amateur are required to be eligible for Photographer of the Year. Computer-generated images and generative AI content of any kind are prohibited and RAW files may be requested for suspect entries. Judging runs August–September 2027 with results due in October. The 2027 prize pool has not yet been announced; the 2026 pool was worth over US$50,000 including US$15,000 cash. — Deadline: July 12, 2027. Fee: $20–$22. Prize: US$1,000 Curator's Award.

item.title: A Land Remembered — Elliott Museum Call for Artists · Historical Society of Martin County
item.description: The Elliott Museum in Stuart, Florida, run by the Historical Society of Martin County, is building a juried contemporary art component into A Land Remembered, an exhibition inspired by Patrick D. Smith's novel of Florida's pioneer era. Photography is named in the call's own media list alongside painting, drawing, watercolour, mixed media, printmaking and sculpture, so documentary and landscape photographers of old Florida - cattle drives and cow hunters, early homesteads, native wildlife, rivers, prairies, hammocks and pine forests, frontier family life - are squarely in scope. Each artist may enter ONE original artwork, existing or new, and must hold the legal right to exhibit and, if applicable, sell it. Generative AI work is barred: artwork created wholly or substantially through generative AI, or whose visual content was generated or substantially altered with it, may not be submitted, while traditional digital tools used on your own original work are permitted. The signed agreement states the door plainly - open to artists of all ages and from all geographic locations, with under-18s entering through a parent or guardian's co-signature. Entry is free and runs in two stages on a JotForm linked from the call page: the Call to Artists agreement first, with contact details, originality and generative-AI certifications and an electronic signature, then the artwork submission itself, which asks for title, year created, medium, dimensions, retail price or NFS, insurance value if requested, one digital image and an artist statement or bio. A selection panel appointed by the Elliott Museum reviews entries after the deadline and notifies everyone by email and phone on 5 November; jury decisions are final and accepted work is inspected again on delivery. Awards are $300 for first place, $200 for second and $100 for third. Count the logistics before you enter: this is a physical show, selected artwork must reach the museum in Stuart by 20 November 2026, 2-D work needs professional presentation and secure hanging hardware (sawtooth hangers are refused), and accepted pieces must stay up for the full run, 2 December 2026 to 30 May 2027 - roughly six months off the wall, whether or not the work sells. Sales are encouraged and run through the museum, which collects the money and forbids side deals: the contract you sign sets the artist's share at 75% of the retail price, though the call page's own summary block advertises 65% - price the work against the contract, and expect payment within 30 days of the museum receiving cleared funds from the buyer. — Deadline: November 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $300 + $200 + $100 + Exhibition.

item.title: Bibin Photography Magazine #7 — Landscape & Identity
item.description: Quarterly contemporary photography magazine from Afghanistan, now at issue 7. The theme is Landscape & Identity, read by guest writer Nasrin Amiri, a photography educator and researcher, through a critical-cultural approach: identity as a fluid perception of the self and its relationship with the surrounding world, shaped by individual and collective memory, social relations, lived experience and the geography of everyday life. The call's own framing rejects landscape photography as the neutral recording of natural reality, treating landscape instead as a human-made construct formed where the photographer's gaze meets memory, belonging or alienation, history and technical choice - so work that reinterprets or argues with a place is the point. Submit 3 to 10 photographs, JPEG or PNG, each file under 3 MB at the highest quality you have for print, named YourName_TitleOfThePhoto.jpg, with the location and date each photograph was taken. No logos, watermarks or frames; no portraits of recognizable individuals, no images containing other artists' work or designs, no identifiable brand elements, no recognizable properties needing an owner's consent, and no merged or juxtaposed frames presented as one image. Rights granted are non-exclusive and limited to Bibin's own magazine, website, social channels and related marketing, with the photographer credited and retaining copyright. Read the compensation clause before you apply: it states plainly that submission and publication are unpaid, and that selected photographers receive no payment, no free print copy and no discount code for the print copy. Each issue's guest writer is free to read the published photographs positively, negatively or neutrally. — Deadline: November 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: TBG+S/TOKAS International Residency Exchange 2027 · Temple Bar Gallery + Studios
item.description: Temple Bar Gallery + Studios in Dublin runs this annual exchange with Tokyo Arts and Space (TOKAS), now in its second year, sending one artist to Tokyo for three months, 1 September to 31 November 2027. The award covers private on-site single-room accommodation and shared studio access at the TOKAS Residency building in Sumida, plus a stipend of 8,000 euro to cover living and working expenses and travel to and from Tokyo. Applications are only accepted from professional practicing visual artists who either live in Ireland or are Irish artists living anywhere in the world, and who are free to travel for the full residency period; lens-based practices are in scope - the 2026 recipient was the Irish artist and filmmaker Patrick Hough. The residency is weighted towards research, reflection and networking rather than production: TOKAS has no production facilities on site, though it connects artists to local workshops, with any associated costs paid by the artist. The shared open-plan studio is partitioned, with designated workspace available 9:30am to 11:00pm. Residents take part in public engagement and professional presentations, culminating in a three-day Open Studio event. Applications are assessed on artistic merit and quality of work relevant to contemporary visual art, motivation, recent work and activity, quality of the proposal and activity plan, and potential for artistic growth. TBG+S shortlists and TOKAS makes the final selection. Artists who have already held this exchange cannot reapply, but unsuccessful past applicants can. The application form on the TBG+S site saves progress for a maximum of 30 days, which is shorter than the open call itself, so starting too early can lose your draft. The cutoff is 5pm, not end of day: the call page reads "Deadline for Applications: Friday 27 November 2026, 5pm". — Deadline: November 27, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: 3-month Tokyo residency + €8,000 stipend.

item.title: CONTACT Photography Festival 2027 — Open Call Exhibitions
item.description:
CONTACT is the annual city-wide photography festival that has taken over Toronto every May since 1997, and its Open Call Exhibitions programme is the part of it that any photographer can walk into. Where the Core Program is produced with museums, major galleries and artist-run centres, the Open Call strand is artist-organised and artist-produced: if you register a fully organised exhibition at a Greater Toronto Area venue before the deadline, you are in the festival. The organisers are explicit that nothing is filtered — "We do not review or jury submissions" — so this is not a competition but a listing and a platform, with your show appearing in the festival's programme and on contactphoto.com alongside the Core Program.
Registration is free and opened on 19 October 2026 for the 31st edition, which runs 1–31 May 2027. CONTACT accepts registrations until 18 January 2027. The programme is open to "emerging and experienced photographers at any career or hobby level", and you do not have to be Toronto-based to take part.
THE ONE HARD CONDITION IS THE VENUE: artists and organisers must secure their own exhibition space before registering, and are responsible for every aspect of production and presentation — CONTACT does not produce, fund or install Open Call shows. Any publicly accessible venue in the GTA counts, including outdoor spaces and storefront windows (the GTA means the City of Toronto plus Durham, Halton, Peel and York Regions; Hamilton is outside it). Exhibition dates must fall wholly or partly within the festival month, and the run can be anything from a single night to more than a month. Registration asks for venue details, accessibility information and opening hours, exhibition title and text, and three images (JPEG or PNG, up to 3000px on the long side, captioned "Artist Name, Title, Year") for the website listing; there is no limit on how many works you actually show. — Deadline: January 18, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: Festival exhibition.

item.title: The James Parker “Open Door” Grant · Artspace Gallery
item.description:
Artspace, the artist-run 501(c)(3) gallery in Richmond, Virginia, has opened a new grant aimed squarely at the artists most open calls price out. The James Parker “Open Door” Fund was established in 2026 in memory of a former Artspace member, through a donation from his widow Beq Parker, and the gallery says the grant is there to “amplify the voices of Richmond, VA artists from all backgrounds, particularly those identifying with underrepresented races and ethnicities, early-career creators, or under-resourced artists”, by removing financial and institutional barriers.
The package is worth over $2,500: up to $2,000 in cash towards project development, equipment, materials and execution; a one-year Artspace Artist Membership with dues waived (valued at $480); at least three one-hour mentorship sessions with a seasoned Artspace artist member covering project management, budgeting and exhibition planning; a place on the Artspace Exhibition Committee in an advisory capacity; and a culminating public event in 2027–28 — a solo exhibition, performance, workshop or open studio hosted or supported by the gallery.
Entry is free and open to artists and creators working in any medium, photography included, with the application deliberately built to avoid gatekeeping: there is no CV or résumé requirement, and selection turns on project potential instead. Applicants send up to five images, media files or web links of recent work, a brief proposal for a project or body of work to be completed in 2027, a resource and support plan, and two narrative answers — how the $2,000 and the gallery's resources would supply what their practice is currently missing, and what next step the year of support would make reachable. THE ONE HARD BAR IS GEOGRAPHIC: applicants must live in the Richmond, VA metropolitan area, and the selected artist has to be local enough to take part in gallery operations, including gallery sitting and Fourth Friday support. Applications close 27 November 2026; portfolios and proposals are reviewed 28 November – 11 December, the top three finalists are interviewed 18–25 December, and the winner and an alternate are announced on 6 January 2027. — Deadline: November 27, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Up to $2,000 + Solo exhibition.
